references.text: The parallel account in Matthew, where the disciples come to Jesus when it is evening and ask him to send the crowd away to buy food in the villages.

The parallel account in Mark, where the disciples point out that it is late and the place is desolate, and ask Jesus to send the people away to buy food for themselves in the surrounding farms and villages.
The parallel account in John, where Jesus asks Philip where they should buy bread for the crowd, and Philip answers that two hundred denarii would not be enough.
A similar situation where Jesus feeds four thousand, and the disciples ask where they can find enough bread in the wilderness to feed such a large crowd.
The parallel to the feeding of the four thousand in Mark, where the crowd has been without food and the disciples wonder how they can get enough bread in the wilderness.
The context verse that tells us Jesus took them to a desolate place near Bethsaida, which explains why the disciples say 'we are in a desolate place'.
The same expression about the day being far spent (ἡ ἡμέρα κέκλικεν) is used by the Emmaus travelers who ask Jesus to stay with them because it is toward evening.
